page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier memory performance, with uncached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 412.91 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 198.33 GB/sec. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21484.0 and a Passmark database operations score of 47617.22. Multi-threaded decompression and software compilation tasks show strong performance, with bzip3 decompression reaching 357.08 GB/sec and Clang compilation scoring 49450.0. In database and web serving workloads, the server demonstrates strong throughput, handling 66.38 million Redis SET operations per second and 71.82 GB/sec in static web serving.

The ARM-based architecture delivers high resource density and memory throughput efficiency, making it a cost-effective option for memory-bound and network-intensive workloads without the premium of x86 licensing. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on network-attached EBS volumes. Additionally, while medium-model LLM text generation is strong at 30.35 tokens/sec, the server exhibits poor performance in small-model text generation at 42.5 tokens/sec and weak prompt processing for large 70B models at 5.9 tokens/sec.

This instance is suited for high-throughput database operations, multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference tasks that benefit from high memory bandwidth and 100 Gbps networking.
